title: November Examination
instructions: This paper consists of FIVE questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Show all calculations and include units.
Drawings may be described in words where you cannot draw on screen.

questions.prompt: In the design process, the first step is to…
Which is a shell structure?
A nutcracker is a…
Two switches connected in parallel give…
Which plastic CANNOT be reshaped once it has set?
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Makes driven gear turn the same way as driver

questions.prompt: Ropes and cables can only resist tension.
In first-angle projection, the top view is drawn above the front view.
What is the name of the force that twists a material?
What is the unit of resistance?
Write a design brief for a stand that holds a cellphone upright on a desk.
questions.memo:
✓ States what will be made (a stand) (1)
✓ For whom (e.g. learners/office workers) (1)
✓ Why / purpose (to hold a phone upright for viewing/charging) (1)

questions.prompt: Give THREE specifications for the cellphone stand.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): holds phones of different sizes; stable/does not tip; allows charging cable; made of strong, light material; costs less than a set amount; attractive

questions.prompt: A cupboard is 1 800 mm tall. How tall will it be on a drawing at a scale of 1 : 20?
State the angles used for (a) isometric and (b) oblique drawings.
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ 30° to the horizontal (1)
(b) ✓ 45° for depth lines (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how triangulation makes a frame structure rigid. Give an example.
questions.memo:
✓ A diagonal member divides a rectangle into triangles (1)
✓ A triangle cannot change shape unless a side breaks (1)
✓ Example: roof truss / pylon / crane / bridge (1)

questions.prompt: Identify the internal force in each: (a) the rope of a tow truck, (b) the legs of a table, (c) a screwdriver being turned, (d) a shelf bracket that sags in the middle.
Explain the difference between a static and a dynamic load, using a bridge as an example.
questions.memo:
✓ Static: the weight of the bridge itself, which does not change (1)
✓ Dynamic: moving cars and wind, which change (1)

questions.prompt: A crowbar lifts a 900 N load placed 0,3 m from the fulcrum. The effort is applied 1,5 m from the fulcrum. Calculate the effort.
Calculate the mechanical advantage of the crowbar in 4.1.
A driver gear with 12 teeth meshes with a driven gear with 36 teeth. If the driver turns at 120 r/min, calculate the speed of the driven gear.
In 4.3, will the driven gear turn faster or slower than the driver, and in which direction?
Name a mechanism that changes rotary motion into linear motion and give ONE use.
questions.memo:
✓ Rack and pinion (1)
✓ Car steering / sliding gate / camera tripod (1)

questions.prompt: Explain why a bicycle uses a chain rather than meshing gears to connect the pedals to the back wheel.
questions.memo:
✓ The sprockets are far apart, and a chain can connect them (1)
✓ It keeps both turning in the same direction without slipping (1)

questions.prompt: A 6 V battery is connected to a resistor of 300 Ω. Calculate the current in amperes.
Draw or describe the truth table for an AND circuit with two switches.
Describe the input, process and output of a doorbell system.
questions.memo:
✓ Input: battery / push-to-make button pressed (1)
✓ Process: switch closes the circuit, wires carry current (1)
✓ Output: buzzer/bell sounds (1)

questions.prompt: Explain THREE safety rules when working with electricity at home.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): do not touch with wet hands; do not overload plugs; replace damaged cords; switch off before repairs; keep appliances away from water; never insert objects into plugs

questions.prompt: A car’s interior light must switch on when EITHER front door is opened. Which logic is this, how are the switches connected, and what type of switch is used?
questions.memo:
✓ OR logic (1)
✓ Switches connected in parallel (1)
✓ Push-to-break switches in the door frames (1)
